answer: Each agent registers one crystal chamber, locks an 80-credit bond, and grows a spiral seed along a temperature curve, filing ring measurements and the chamber nadir reading. An auditor remeasures the crystal, matches rings to the curve and nadir to the log, and burns the bond on mismatch, reuse, or missing rings. Chamber 1 costs 28, the k-th 28+9(k-1), the 1000th 9019, so 1,000 fakes pay 4,523,500 plus 80,000 locked, each needing its own seed and heater. A rented-chamber ring fails: one seed cannot yield two spiral patterns at once. An honest agent pays 28 once and keeps its bond after audit.
